scene.label: Act 4, Scene 2
scene.title: SCENE II. London. A Room of State in the Palace
scene.location: London. A Room of State in the Palace

content.text: The trumpets sound a sennet. Enter Richard in pomp, Buckingham, Catesby, Ratcliffe, Lovell, a Page and others.

lines.text: Stand all apart. Cousin of Buckingham!
lines.plainText: Stand all apart Cousin of Buckingham

lines.text: My gracious sovereign!
lines.plainText: My gracious sovereign

lines.text: Give me thy hand.
lines.plainText: Give me thy hand

content.text: [Here he ascendeth the throne. Sound trumpets.]

lines.text: Still live they, and for ever let them last!
lines.plainText: Still live they and for ever let them last

lines.text: Ah, Buckingham, now do I play the touch,
lines.plainText: Ah Buckingham now do I play the touch

lines.text: To try if thou be current gold indeed.
lines.plainText: To try if thou be current gold indeed

lines.text: Young Edward lives; think now what I would speak.
lines.plainText: Young Edward lives think now what I would speak

lines.text: Say on, my loving lord.
lines.plainText: Say on my loving lord

lines.text: Why, Buckingham, I say I would be King.
lines.plainText: Why Buckingham I say I would be King

lines.text: Why, so you are, my thrice-renowned lord.
lines.plainText: Why so you are my thricerenowned lord

lines.text: Ha! Am I King? 'Tis so—but Edward lives.
lines.plainText: Ha Am I King 'Tis sobut Edward lives

lines.text: True, noble Prince.
lines.plainText: True noble Prince

lines.text: O bitter consequence,
lines.plainText: O bitter consequence

lines.text: That Edward still should live "true noble prince!"
lines.plainText: That Edward still should live true noble prince

lines.text: Cousin, thou wast not wont to be so dull.
lines.plainText: Cousin thou wast not wont to be so dull

lines.text: Shall I be plain? I wish the bastards dead,
lines.plainText: Shall I be plain I wish the bastards dead

lines.text: And I would have it suddenly performed.
lines.plainText: And I would have it suddenly performed

lines.text: What sayst thou now? Speak suddenly, be brief.
lines.plainText: What sayst thou now Speak suddenly be brief

lines.text: Your Grace may do your pleasure.
lines.plainText: Your Grace may do your pleasure

lines.text: Tut, tut, thou art all ice; thy kindness freezes.
lines.plainText: Tut tut thou art all ice thy kindness freezes

lines.text: Say, have I thy consent that they shall die?
lines.plainText: Say have I thy consent that they shall die

lines.text: Give me some little breath, some pause, dear lord,
lines.plainText: Give me some little breath some pause dear lord

lines.text: Before I positively speak in this.
lines.plainText: Before I positively speak in this

lines.text: I will resolve you herein presently.
lines.plainText: I will resolve you herein presently

lines.text: [Aside.] The King is angry. See, he gnaws his lip.
lines.plainText: Aside The King is angry See he gnaws his lip

lines.text: [Aside.] I will converse with iron-witted fools
lines.plainText: Aside I will converse with ironwitted fools

lines.text: And unrespective boys; none are for me
lines.plainText: And unrespective boys none are for me

lines.text: That look into me with considerate eyes.
lines.plainText: That look into me with considerate eyes

lines.text: High-reaching Buckingham grows circumspect.
lines.plainText: Highreaching Buckingham grows circumspect

lines.text: Boy!
lines.plainText: Boy

lines.text: My lord?
lines.plainText: My lord

lines.text: Know'st thou not any whom corrupting gold
lines.plainText: Know'st thou not any whom corrupting gold

lines.text: Will tempt unto a close exploit of death?
lines.plainText: Will tempt unto a close exploit of death

lines.text: I know a discontented gentleman
lines.plainText: I know a discontented gentleman

lines.text: Whose humble means match not his haughty spirit.
lines.plainText: Whose humble means match not his haughty spirit

lines.text: Gold were as good as twenty orators,
lines.plainText: Gold were as good as twenty orators

lines.text: And will, no doubt, tempt him to anything.
lines.plainText: And will no doubt tempt him to anything

lines.text: What is his name?
lines.plainText: What is his name

lines.text: His name, my lord, is Tyrrel.
lines.plainText: His name my lord is Tyrrel

lines.text: I partly know the man. Go, call him hither, boy.
lines.plainText: I partly know the man Go call him hither boy

lines.text: Know, my loving lord,
lines.plainText: Know my loving lord

lines.text: The Marquess Dorset, as I hear, is fled
lines.plainText: The Marquess Dorset as I hear is fled

lines.text: To Richmond, in the parts where he abides.
lines.plainText: To Richmond in the parts where he abides

lines.text: Come hither, Catesby. Rumour it abroad
lines.plainText: Come hither Catesby Rumour it abroad

lines.text: That Anne my wife is very grievous sick;
lines.plainText: That Anne my wife is very grievous sick

lines.text: I will take order for her keeping close.
lines.plainText: I will take order for her keeping close

lines.text: Inquire me out some mean poor gentleman,
lines.plainText: Inquire me out some mean poor gentleman

lines.text: Whom I will marry straight to Clarence' daughter.
lines.plainText: Whom I will marry straight to Clarence' daughter

lines.text: The boy is foolish, and I fear not him.
lines.plainText: The boy is foolish and I fear not him

lines.text: Look how thou dream'st! I say again, give out
lines.plainText: Look how thou dream'st I say again give out

lines.text: That Anne, my Queen, is sick and like to die.
lines.plainText: That Anne my Queen is sick and like to die

lines.text: About it, for it stands me much upon
lines.plainText: About it for it stands me much upon

lines.text: To stop all hopes whose growth may damage me.
lines.plainText: To stop all hopes whose growth may damage me

lines.text: James Tyrrel, and your most obedient subject.
lines.plainText: James Tyrrel and your most obedient subject

lines.text: Art thou indeed?
lines.plainText: Art thou indeed

lines.text: Prove me, my gracious lord.
lines.plainText: Prove me my gracious lord

lines.text: Dar'st thou resolve to kill a friend of mine?
lines.plainText: Dar'st thou resolve to kill a friend of mine

lines.text: Please you. But I had rather kill two enemies.
lines.plainText: Please you But I had rather kill two enemies

lines.text: Why then thou hast it; two deep enemies,
lines.plainText: Why then thou hast it two deep enemies

lines.text: Foes to my rest, and my sweet sleep's disturbers,
lines.plainText: Foes to my rest and my sweet sleep's disturbers

lines.text: Are they that I would have thee deal upon.
lines.plainText: Are they that I would have thee deal upon

lines.text: Tyrell, I mean those bastards in the Tower.
lines.plainText: Tyrell I mean those bastards in the Tower

lines.text: Let me have open means to come to them,
lines.plainText: Let me have open means to come to them

lines.text: And soon I'll rid you from the fear of them.
lines.plainText: And soon I'll rid you from the fear of them

lines.text: Thou sing'st sweet music. Hark, come hither, Tyrrel.
lines.plainText: Thou sing'st sweet music Hark come hither Tyrrel

lines.text: Go, by this token. Rise, and lend thine ear.
lines.plainText: Go by this token Rise and lend thine ear

lines.text: [Whispers.] There is no more but so. Say it is done,
lines.plainText: Whispers There is no more but so Say it is done

lines.text: And I will love thee, and prefer thee for it.
lines.plainText: And I will love thee and prefer thee for it

lines.text: I will dispatch it straight.
lines.plainText: I will dispatch it straight

lines.text: My lord, I have considered in my mind
lines.plainText: My lord I have considered in my mind

lines.text: The late request that you did sound me in.
lines.plainText: The late request that you did sound me in

lines.text: Well, let that rest. Dorset is fled to Richmond.
lines.plainText: Well let that rest Dorset is fled to Richmond

lines.text: I hear the news, my lord.
lines.plainText: I hear the news my lord

lines.text: Stanley, he is your wife's son. Well, look unto it.
lines.plainText: Stanley he is your wife's son Well look unto it

lines.text: My lord, I claim the gift, my due by promise,
lines.plainText: My lord I claim the gift my due by promise

lines.text: For which your honour and your faith is pawned:
lines.plainText: For which your honour and your faith is pawned

lines.text: Th' earldom of Hereford, and the movables
lines.plainText: Th' earldom of Hereford and the movables

lines.text: Which you have promised I shall possess.
lines.plainText: Which you have promised I shall possess

lines.text: Stanley, look to your wife. If she convey
lines.plainText: Stanley look to your wife If she convey

lines.text: Letters to Richmond, you shall answer it.
lines.plainText: Letters to Richmond you shall answer it

lines.text: What says your Highness to my just request?
lines.plainText: What says your Highness to my just request

lines.text: I do remember me, Henry the Sixth
lines.plainText: I do remember me Henry the Sixth

lines.text: Did prophesy that Richmond should be King,
lines.plainText: Did prophesy that Richmond should be King

lines.text: When Richmond was a little peevish boy.
lines.plainText: When Richmond was a little peevish boy

lines.text: A king perhaps—
lines.plainText: A king perhaps

lines.text: My lord—
lines.plainText: My lord

lines.text: How chance the prophet could not at that time
lines.plainText: How chance the prophet could not at that time

lines.text: Have told me, I being by, that I should kill him?
lines.plainText: Have told me I being by that I should kill him

lines.text: My lord, your promise for the earldom—
lines.plainText: My lord your promise for the earldom

lines.text: Richmond! When last I was at Exeter,
lines.plainText: Richmond When last I was at Exeter

lines.text: The Mayor in courtesy showed me the castle
lines.plainText: The Mayor in courtesy showed me the castle

lines.text: And called it Rougemount, at which name I started,
lines.plainText: And called it Rougemount at which name I started

lines.text: Because a bard of Ireland told me once
lines.plainText: Because a bard of Ireland told me once

lines.text: I should not live long after I saw Richmond.
lines.plainText: I should not live long after I saw Richmond

lines.text: My lord—
lines.plainText: My lord

lines.text: Ay, what's o'clock?
lines.plainText: Ay what's o'clock

lines.text: I am thus bold to put your Grace in mind
lines.plainText: I am thus bold to put your Grace in mind

lines.text: Of what you promised me.
lines.plainText: Of what you promised me

lines.text: Well, but what's o'clock?
lines.plainText: Well but what's o'clock

lines.text: Upon the stroke of ten.
lines.plainText: Upon the stroke of ten

lines.text: Well, let it strike.
lines.plainText: Well let it strike

lines.text: Why let it strike?
lines.plainText: Why let it strike

lines.text: Because that, like a jack, thou keep'st the stroke
lines.plainText: Because that like a jack thou keep'st the stroke

lines.text: Betwixt thy begging and my meditation.
lines.plainText: Betwixt thy begging and my meditation

lines.text: I am not in the giving vein today.
lines.plainText: I am not in the giving vein today

lines.text: Why then, resolve me whether you will or no.
lines.plainText: Why then resolve me whether you will or no

lines.text: Thou troublest me; I am not in the vein.
lines.plainText: Thou troublest me I am not in the vein

lines.text: And is it thus? Repays he my deep service
lines.plainText: And is it thus Repays he my deep service

lines.text: With such contempt? Made I him King for this?
lines.plainText: With such contempt Made I him King for this

lines.text: O, let me think on Hastings, and be gone
lines.plainText: O let me think on Hastings and be gone

lines.text: To Brecknock while my fearful head is on!
lines.plainText: To Brecknock while my fearful head is on
